title: Lead Business Analyst
description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role

We're looking for a Lead Technical Business Analyst to play a pivotal role in shaping the future of change delivery across the FT's Product & Technology organisation.

Reporting into the Portfolio & Programmes team, you'll lead the assessment, discovery and technical analysis of new initiatives entering our change portfolio. Working closely with stakeholders across Product, Technology, Data and the wider business, you'll ensure ideas are well understood, appropriately scoped and assessed for feasibility, complexity and delivery readiness before they progress into prioritisation and planning.

As the lead business analyst within the portfolio function, you'll establish best practice for business analysis, mentor other analysts and act as a trusted advisor, helping teams make informed investment and delivery decisions that support the FT's strategic objectives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the assessment and triage of new change initiatives entering the Product & Technology portfolio.
  • Facilitate discovery workshops to understand business needs, define outcomes and clarify requirements.
  • Produce high-quality business, functional and non-functional requirements that support successful solution design.
  • Partner with Product Managers, Architects, Engineers and Delivery teams to assess solution options, technical feasibility and delivery complexity.
  • Identify risks, dependencies, assumptions and implementation constraints early in the change lifecycle.
  • Support business case development, investment decisions and portfolio prioritisation with clear analysis and recommendations.
  • Contribute to portfolio planning by providing insights into delivery effort, resource requirements and roadmap sequencing.
  • Build trusted relationships across Product, Technology, Editorial, Commercial, Data and Corporate teams.
  • Define and champion business analysis standards, tools and best practices across the organisation.
  • Coach and mentor other Business Analysts while driving continuous improvement across portfolio intake and discovery processes.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Significant experience as a Senior or Lead Business Analyst within technology, digital product or transformation environments.
  • Extensive experience leading discovery, requirements gathering and solution assessment activities.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex business and technical challenges into clear, actionable requirements.
  • Experience working closely with engineering, architecture, product and delivery teams throughout the change lifecycle.
  • Strong understanding of software development lifecycles, systems integration and modern technology platforms.
  • Experience supporting business cases, investment decisions and portfolio planning.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to influence at all levels.

Desirable

  • Experience within media, publishing, digital subscription or technology-led organisations.
  • Experience supporting portfolio management, governance or demand management functions.
  • Knowledge of Agile, Lean delivery approaches and modern product operating models.
  • Exposure to enterprise architecture, cloud technologies or data platforms.

What's in it for You?

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments or personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements, or have any questions, please send an email to talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Further Information

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process may be monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

Please beware of fraudulent job postings and offers claiming to be from the Financial Times. All legitimate opportunities will direct you to apply through the official Financial Times careers site, and the FT will never ask for financial information, payments, or referrals to third parties during the hiring process. If you have any concerns about the legitimacy of a job posting or suspect any scam activity, please contact talent@ft.com.

  • Uses developmentally appropriate play as a primary tool in assessing and meeting psychosocial needs.

  • Utilizes therapeutic play and other creative modalities to meet individual development and emotional needs.

**Therapeutic play refers to specialized activities that are developmentally supportive and facilitate the emotional well-being of a pediatric patient. Therapeutic play typically consists of at least one of the following types of activities: 1) the encouragement of emotional expression (e.g. reenactment of experiences through healthcare play), 2) instructional play to educate children about medical experiences, and 3) physiologically enhancing play (e.g. blowing bubbles to improve breathing).

  • Creates an environment where play is valued and encouraged.

  • Prepares and maintains a safe, inviting, and developmentally responsive play environment appropriate for patients and families.

  • Plans and implements varied developmentally supportive activities.

  • Applies formal and informal assessment techniques to assess psychosocial needs, and continue cyclical process of assessment, plan, intervention, and evaluation.

  • Assesses patient and family knowledge level, misconceptions, previous experience, and unique social, cultural, and learning needs.

  • Assesses patient and family responses to stress.

  • Supports the central role of the family, valuing strengths, and needs; works to maintain family units.

  • Utilizes effective communication skills in the process of supporting children and families.

  • Provides support to siblings, parents, and other friends and family members in order to improve understanding of the patient’s situation and familiarization with the health care environment.

  • Paces interactions in response to a child’s and family’s lead.

  • Demonstrates respect for diversity.

  • Participates in interdisciplinary care conferences, psychosocial rounds, and nursing report.

  • Maintains good interpersonal relations with patients, families, visitors, and other employees, following departmental and hospital-wide philosophy.

  • Communicates concisely with others, integrating theory and evidence-based practice to obtain and share pertinent information.

  • Provides input about facility design and provisions to promote orientation, comfort, healing, security, and normalization.

  • Ensures that the department’s resources, playrooms, and activity areas are maintained appropriately and cleaned per hospital guidelines, adhering to MoPH standards.

  • Ensures that infection control procedures are adhered to at all times and provides assistance to the Department in this regard. This would include wiping down table surfaces, toy washing, and acting as liaison with Housekeeping and Infection Control staff.

Essential Function 2

Provides teaching for and assists with potentially stressful patient and family health care events:

  • Utilizes knowledge of child development (neonate to adolescent) and family-centered care to:
    • Design and implement child life interventions including age-appropriate preparation and education and procedural support.

    • Plan and implement teaching and support accordingly.

  • Provides psychological preparation, incorporating key elements of developmentally appropriate information, encouragement of emotional expression, and the formation of a trusting relationship.

  • Uses accurate and developmentally appropriate teaching aids and techniques.

  • Recognizes verbal and non-verbal cues and adapts accordingly.

  • Uses minimally threatening, developmentally supportive language.

  • Describes sensory information, sequence, timing, and duration of events.

  • Facilitates planning, rehearsal, and implementation of coping strategies.

  • Facilitates opportunities for play to decrease distress and increase effective coping.

  • Utilizes appropriate psychological pain management strategies, and advocates for additional intervention as needed.

  • Considers the unique needs of the child and family, such as coping style, previous experience, developmental level, culture, spirituality, family situation, and emotional state.

Essential Function 3

Represent, communicate, and teach Child Life services appropriately to other professionals, volunteers, students, and the community; work collaboratively with all parties as needed to achieve optimal outcomes:

  • Demonstrates effective advocacy for Child Life practice, emotional safety, and psychosocial issues.

  • Integrates interdisciplinary goals into Child Life services.

  • Communicates expectations and roles clearly and concisely.

  • Creates concise, objective, and accurate clinical notes, documenting information pertinent to the plan of care in alignment with documentation guidelines.

  • Recommends consults or referrals when circumstances are beyond the scope of Child Life practice.

  • Maintains professional presentation of self, including careful attention to verbal and written communication, as well as standards in dress code.

  • Provides comprehensive orientation to services.

  • Assesses and responds to diverse learning needs.

  • Provides a safe learning and working environment.

  • Demonstrates respect for the viewpoints of others.

  • Models professionalism at all times.

  • Provides orientation to department, assigned patient care areas, and hospital in general to observers, students, volunteers, Child Life Specialist I’s, and Child Life Assistants.

  • Creates, facilitates, and leads modules and learning opportunities for child life students.

  • Prepares expectations, goals, and plans for student rotation on assigned unit in coordination with the Internship Coordinator/Leadership, and guides students through learning experiences as assigned.

  • While directly supervising a student rotation, provides daily assignments, evaluates their work, and provides resources necessary.

  • Communicates assessments, projects, and work completed to Child Life Supervisor and Manager on an ongoing basis.

  • Attends and participates in assigned meetings.

  • Leads or participates in priority initiatives and education.

  • Pursues, participates in and leads scholarly activities (publications, research, quality improvement, presentations, etc.) to advance the Child Life profession and best practices.

  • Develops and assists in facilitation of department-wide professional development activities including journal clubs, clinical supervision groups, and educational sessions.

  • Adheres to Sidra’s standards as they appear in the Code of Conduct and Conflict of Interest policies.

  • Adheres to and promotes Sidra’s Values

Essential Function 4

Provides leadership, facilitating successful department performance and quality improvement:

  • Leads by example and displays respect for, commitment to, and pride in department and facility.

  • Demonstrates vast knowledge of the Child Life profession, Child Life Department, and Patient and Family Centered Care Principles.

  • Prioritizes patient and family care needs across areas/teams as needed; takes action to mobilize teammates to address identified needs.

  • Demonstrates positive initiative, flexibility, and reliability in accepting and adapting to change and direction at all times.

  • Problem solves daily challenges; effectively communicates with and guides teammates in achieving optimal outcomes.

  • Demonstrates effective time management skills, balancing patient care needs with leadership tasks.

  • Identifies and leads priority department and hospital initiatives, workgroups, and education to improve effectiveness, efficiency, and quality of services delivered to patients and families.

  • Acts as a role model and mentor to new Child Life employees through teaching, observing, assessing, and validating skills and competencies.

  • Demonstrates and shares high level of expertise in Child Life skill set and Sidra Medicine patient care practices.

In view of the evolving needs and opportunities within Sidra, this position may be required to perform other duties as assigned and reporting relationships may vary.

QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS –REQUIREMENTS

ESSENTIAL

Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Child Life or Play Therapy, or Leisure Studies, or Child Development, Child and Family Studies, or Family Centered Care or Human Development or Sociology, or Psychology, or Therapeutic Recreation, or Expressive Arts, or Creative Arts Therapy, or Family Systems, or Social Work, or Early Childhood Education, or Education, or Public Health or Health Care Administration or similarly titled degree; Foundational courses in Child Life, Child Development, and Hospital Play

Experience

  • 5+ years clinical experience as Certified Child Life Specialist or Registered Hospital/Health Play Specialist in pediatric settings
  • Strong clinical expertise across the competencies of the Child Life field
  • Experience in Child Life/Hospital Play department leadership/supervisory roles/responsibilities.

Certification and Licensure

  • Child Life Specialist Certification (CCLS) via the Association of Child Life Professionals (formerly Child Life Council, Inc). or Healthcare Play Specialist Education Trust (HPSET) Registration; or Registered Hospital Play Specialist (RegHPS) via the Hospital Play Specialists Association of Aotearoa/New Zealand (Inc.)

  • Eligibility for Licensure in the State of Qatar

Professional Membership

Member of the Association of Child Life Professionals (ACLP), National Association for Health Play Specialist (UK), and/or Hospital Play Specialist Association (NZ)

Job Specific Skills and Abilities

  • Demonstrated knowledge of Child Life Specialist principles and practices.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of best practices in Child Life specialty
  • Effective teaching, mentoring, and supervisory skills
  • Experience in organizing data and generating thorough, accurate, timely reports.
  • Ability to provide assessments regarding developmental reactions to hospitalization and risk for stress potential.
  • Ability to design and implement interventions to meet individual patient and family needs.
  • Ability to function as a collaborative member of the interdisciplinary team and communicate and advocate for patient/family needs within this team.
  • Ability to effectively supervise staff through positive leadership skills and provide consistent and supportive feedback for personal and program improvement.
  • Ability to make leadership decisions to simultaneously provide the best patient care and support hospital-wide strategic plans.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks including direct clinical work and administrative responsibilities.
  • Experience in organizing data and generating thorough, accurate, timely reports.
  • Effective team member.
  • Effective interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Leadership skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite
  • Fluency in written and spoken English

title: Senior Digital Experience & UX Executive
description:
Description

Workplace: White City, London - 3 days a week in the office

The role

As Senior Digital Experience & UX Executive, you'll play a key role in shaping how buyers discover, experience and engage with one of the world’s largest television catalogues. Working across Marketing, Product and Technology, you'll continuously improve customer journeys through user-centred design, customer insight and product optimisation.

You'll own small to medium-sized product initiatives, support larger strategic programmes, and work closely with Marketing, Sales, Technology and Content teams to deliver digital experiences that support commercial growth.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys combining product thinking, user experience, customer insight and creativity to solve customer problems and shape the future of ITV Studios' digital experiences.

Main responsibilities

Championing the user, collaborating closely with the Senior Digital Product Manager, Technology Manager, and development squad, ensuring our designs are innovative, effective, and deeply user-centred with highly engaging user journeys. Your duties will include:

  • Strategic Design: Own the end-to-end design process, from deep user research and problem definition to high-fidelity mock-ups, requirements definition (as Epics and User Stories) and developer hand-off and subsequent QA testing. Be the voice of the customer, articulating design decisions through user insight, commercial value and evidence-based recommendations.
  • Collaborative Agile Squad Integration: Thrive within an agile product squad, balancing user needs with commercial business objectives. Work seamlessly with product owners, technology teams and development partners, ensuring smooth design implementation and high quality delivery.
  • Systematic & User-Centric Approach: Apply a rigorous, systematic approach to design, leveraging our existing design system and partners. Iterate based on user feedback, ensuring the product is intuitive, accessible, and commercially effective and engaging.

Catalogue Experience & Optimisation

  • Own the continuous optimisation of the ITV Studios Catalogue Experience across itvstudios.com and Watch Anywhere.
  • Champion customer-first thinking and shape editorial experiences that improve discovery, engagement and commercial impact.
  • Support the evolution of homepage experiences, genre destinations, collections and programme pages, ensuring the catalogue continues to evolve alongside changing customer needs and commercial priorities.
  • Partner with Marketing, Sales & Product teams to develop best practice for customer journeys, digital merchandising and catalogue experiences.
  • Identify opportunities to improve customer journeys through experimentation, customer insight and UX thinking.
  • Balance UX best practice with strong editorial judgement, ensuring customer journeys reflect commercial priorities while maintaining a premium catalogue experience.

UX, Product Design & Delivery

  • Champion user-centred design across ITV Studios' digital products.
  • Create wireframes, customer journeys, prototypes and user flows that support new product initiatives and continuous improvement.
  • Manage project plans, timelines and stakeholder communication throughout delivery.
  • Support larger strategic programmes led by the Digital Products Manager, taking ownership of individual workstreams while contributing to sprint planning, backlog refinement and roadmap execution.

Product Quality & Optimisation

  • Own quality assurance across ITV Studios' digital products, ensuring new functionality is thoroughly tested prior to release.
  • Coordinate functional, regression and user acceptance testing, troubleshoot issues and support successful product releases.
  • Use analytics, customer behaviour and user research to identify opportunities that improve customer engagement and product performance.
  • Translate insight into recommendations that influence future roadmap priorities.

Catalogue Content Strategy

  • Champion structured catalogue content, metadata and editorial quality, supporting Catalogue Content Excellence and future Content Hub integration to improve content quality, reduce duplication and create shared value across the business.
  • Work collaboratively with Marketing, Content and Technology teams to improve content governance and support a connected catalogue ecosystem.
  • Support initiatives that improve reusable content, metadata and system integration.

  • Own the end-to-end delivery of small to medium-sized product initiatives, managing requirements, timelines, stakeholders, testing and successful implementation

Collaboration & Innovation

  • Act as the customer experience champion throughout product development, ensuring every enhancement improves the buyer journey while supporting commercial objectives.
  • Build strong relationships across Marketing, Sales, Technology and Content to deliver connected digital experiences.
  • Champion collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement, bringing fresh thinking and emerging technologies into future product development.

Skills you’ll need (minimum criteria)

  • Proven experience designing customer-facing digital experiences, ideally within a B2B, SaaS, media or content-rich environment.
  • A compelling portfolio showcasing your expertise in end-to-end Product Design & Delivery, highlighting problem-solving, user-centricity, simplicity and visual excellence.
  • Experience working on websites, digital products or customer-facing digital experiences.
  • Strong UX knowledge and expertise in user-centred design, accessibility and responsive design.
  • Proficiency in design, wireframing and prototyping tools (Figma or similar).
  • Experience delivering digital projects or product enhancements from concept through to implementation.
  • Experience managing quality assurance, usability testing and product testing.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate customer insight into product improvements.
  • Experience working collaboratively within cross-functional product teams to deliver customer-focused digital products that support commercial growth.
  • Experience coordinating multiple workstreams and managing competing priorities.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication and presentation skills.
  • A creative, curious and innovative mindset with a passion for design, technology and continuously improving customer experiences.

Other things we’re looking for (key criteria)

  • Experience working within Agile product teams (Scrum/Kanban).
  • Experience using Jira, Confluence or similar product management tools.
  • Knowledge of GA4, digital analytics or product analytics.
  • Understanding of CMS platforms, structured content and metadata.
  • Experience using Google Workspace productivity tools.
  • Experience using a range of modern design and prototyping tools.
  • Experience working with AI-enabled tools and emerging digital technologies.
  • Interest in television, streaming or entertainment.

Why Join Us:

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the future of one of the world’s largest television catalogues. You'll work at the intersection of Product, Marketing and Technology, influencing how global buyers discover and engage with world-class content while helping define the next generation of ITV Studios’ digital products.

title: Fire Alarm Service Engineer
description:
Job Description

Fire Alarm Service Engineer – Static Site (Kent)

About Us:

Johnson Controls, a global leader in thermal management, mission-critical building systems, energy efficiency, and decarbonization, helps customers use energy more productively, reduce carbon emissions, and operate with the precision and resilience required in rapidly expanding industries such as data centers, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, advanced manufacturing, and higher education.


For more than 140 years, Johnson Controls has delivered performance where it really matters. Backed by advanced technology, lifecycle services and an industry-leading field organization, we elevate customer performance, turn goals into real-world results and help move society forward.

What You Will Do

Johnson Controls is hiring a Fire Alarm Service Engineer for a static on-site role at a major facility in Ashford, Kent. We are seeking a candidate with strong experience in fire alarm systems, along with a willingness to develop further in gas suppression technologies.

You will join a dedicated on-site team responsible for the servicing, preventative maintenance, routine servicing, fault-finding, and remedial works associated with site-wide fire detection, gas suppression, and passive/mechanical fire protection systems. Daily client interaction is required to ensure smooth operations, clear communication, and adherence to strict site safety and operational protocols.

Typical systems include:

  • Conventional & addressable fire detection and alarm systems
  • Networked systems and graphical interfaces
  • Gas extinguishing systems (Argonite, CO2, Inergen, Novec)
  • Mechanical fire suppression equipment

You will take personal ownership of service delivery, quality, and safety, acting as a role model for best practice and advising the client on remedial actions and potential system upgrades.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and commission scheme
  • Overtime rates and door-to-door travel time
  • Call-out rota payment
  • Engineer incentive plan
  • Company vehicle, fuel card, and full PPE
  • 25 days paid holiday plus bank holidays, with the option to purchase additional days
  • Paid sick leave
  • Matched pension contributions, life assurance, and employee assistance programme
  • Discounts on high street brands and Johnson Controls security products
  • Cycle-to-work scheme and employee referral scheme
  • Access to business resource groups
  • Extensive on-the-job and cross-training opportunities with outstanding resources
  • Training on Johnson Controls values, systems, and products
  • All equipment required to complete your work
  • Long-term career development and progression pathways
  • Supportive, collaborative team environment promoting work–life balance and wellbeing

How You Will Do It

  • Service, maintain, and fault-find on fire detection and fire alarm systems
  • Receive training and development in gas suppression and mechanical suppression systems
  • Carry out integrity testing (training provided if required)
  • Complete all service documentation accurately using an iPad and service software
  • Liaise with the client to obtain permits to work and ensure compliance with site procedures
  • Attend mandatory training and maintain required certifications
  • Support occasional mechanical and passive fire protection tasks
  • Participate in the on-call rota on a rotating weekly basis
  • Identify, escalate, and report health and safety concerns promptly
  • Conform to all QEHS regulations and contribute to a zero-harm workplace
  • Sign onto RAMS, PPE requirements, toolbox talks, van audits, and accident investigations
  • Take part in internal technical audits and continuous improvement activities
  • Coach and support apprentices and new starters
  • Act as a key link between the client and the Field Line Manager, ensuring clear communication of completed works and outstanding actions
  • Represent Johnson Controls with professionalism, accountability, and inclusivity

What We Look For

Required

  • Proven experience working with fire detection and fire alarm systems
  • Experience within a service-focused business
  • Good understanding of gas suppression systems and their maintenance
  • Technical knowledge of fire legislation, standards, and associated field devices
  • Integrity testing experience (or willingness to train)
  • Excellent communication and customer service skills
  • Strong IT literacy
  • Full UK driving licence
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Willingness to travel for training
  • Ability to participate in the out-of-hours callout rota
  • Ability to pass enhanced security vetting (Disclosure Scotland, enhanced screening, high-security site checks)

Desirable

  • Experience coaching or developing others
  • Experience working on high-hazard or critical-infrastructure sites
